content:
## Introduction & Recruitment Overview

The Staff Selection Commission General Duty (**SSC GD**) Constable examination is India's largest paramilitary recruitment drive, selecting tens of thousands of young candidates (10th pass) into the **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs)**, National Investigation Agency, and Special Security Group. These forces include:
- **BSF** (Border Security Force)
- **CISF** (Central Industrial Security Force)
- **CRPF** (Central Reserve Police Force)
- **ITBP** (Indo-Tibetan Border Police)
- **SSB** (Sashastra Seema Bal)
- **Assam Rifles (AR)**
- **SSF** (Secretariat Security Force)
- **NCB** (Narcotics Control Bureau - Sepoy)

SSC GD offers central government job security, pension benefits (NPS), medical facilities at Central Armed Police hospitals, ration allowances, risk & hardship allowances for border and high-altitude deployments, and 7th Central Pay Commission compensation.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> **Bilingual Exam Option in 13 Regional Languages**: In addition to Hindi and English, the Computer Based Examination (CBE) for SSC GD is conducted in 13 regional Indian languages (Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu), making it accessible for aspirants across all states!

## Step-by-Step Selection Procedure

1. **Computer Based Examination (CBE)**: 80 multiple choice questions for 160 marks (60 minutes).
2. **Physical Standard Test (PST)**: Measurement of height and chest by biometric scanning devices.
3. **Physical Efficiency Test (PET)**: 5 km race for male candidates and 1.6 km race for female candidates within designated time limits.
4. **Detailed Medical Examination (DME) & Document Verification (DV)**: Physical and medical fitness assessment by CAPF Medical Boards.
5. **Review Medical Examination (RME)**: Fast-track second opinion examination for medically appealed candidates within 24–48 hours.
6. **All India Merit List & Force Allocation**: Candidates are allocated to forces based on their normalized marks and preference order.

## Computer Based Examination (CBE) Pattern & Weightage Graph

The CBE has **80 questions** carrying **2 marks each** (Total 160 marks), to be attempted in **60 minutes**. There is a negative marking of **0.25 marks** for each wrong response.

| Section / Subject | Questions | Marks | Mark Weightage Graph | Sectional Nature |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Part A: General Intelligence & Reasoning** | 20 Questions | 40 Marks | [BAR:25%:Reasoning] | Logic, Puzzles, Coding-Decoding, Non-Verbal Figures |
| **Part B: General Knowledge & General Awareness** | 20 Questions | 40 Marks | [BAR:25%:General Awareness] | Static GK, General Science, Indian History, Geography, Polity, Current Affairs |
| **Part C: Elementary Mathematics** | 20 Questions | 40 Marks | [BAR:25%:Elementary Maths] | Arithmetic, Number Systems, Mensuration, Percentages, Ratio, Work & Time |
| **Part D: English OR Hindi (Optional Choice)** | 20 Questions | 40 Marks | [BAR:25%:Language (Hindi/Eng)] | Basic Grammar, Comprehension, Vocabulary, Error Spotting |
| **Total Composite Examination** | **80 Questions** | **160 Marks** | **[BAR:100%:Total Test]** | **Composite Time: 60 Minutes (Negative Marking: 0.25 marks)** |

> [!TIP]  
> **Language Option Freedom**: In Part D, you can choose between **Hindi** and **English** at the start of the exam regardless of your application form preference. Over 80% of candidates in North/Central India score 36+/40 in the Hindi section by mastering basic sandhi, samas, muhavare, and vilom shabd!

## Granular Topic-Wise Syllabus Breakdown

### 1. General Intelligence & Reasoning (20 Questions / 40 Marks)
- **Analogies & Classification**: Semantic, number, and figurative analogies.
- **Coding and Decoding**: Letter substitution, matrix codes, number patterns.
- **Series Completion**: Number series, alphabet chains, alpha-numeric series.
- **Spatial Visualization & Orientation**: Paper folding, paper cutting, mirror and water images.
- **Relationship Concepts**: Family tree problems, coded blood relationships.
- **Arithmetic Reasoning & Figural Classification**: Mathematical operational symbols, venn diagrams.
- **Visual Memory & Non-Verbal**: Embedded figures, pattern completion, dice and cubes.

### 2. General Knowledge & General Awareness (20 Questions / 40 Marks)
- **India and Neighboring Countries**: Capital cities, currencies, international borders, bilateral agreements.
- **History & Heritage**: Ancient, Medieval, and Modern Indian history, freedom movement leaders, historical battles.
- **Culture & Arts**: Classical and folk dance forms, musical instruments, regional festivals, traditional paintings.
- **Geography**: Mountain ranges, major rivers, dams, sanctuaries, soil classification, seasons.
- **Indian Polity & Constitution**: Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, Parliamentary system, constitutional articles.
- **Indian Economy**: Banking basics, GST, five-year plans, agricultural crops (Kharif, Rabi, Zaid).
- **General Science**: Everyday science concepts up to 10th level (Physics, Chemistry, Biology).
- **Sports & Awards**: National awards (Bharat Ratna, Padma Awards), Olympic games, cricket, athletics.

### 3. Elementary Mathematics (20 Questions / 40 Marks)
- **Number Systems & Computation of Whole Numbers**: Divisibility, prime numbers, factors.
- **Decimals and Fractions**: VBODMAS rules, basic algebraic simplification.
- **Relationship Between Numbers**: LCM, HCF, finding common multiples.
- **Fundamental Arithmetical Operations**: Percentages, Ratio and Proportion, Averages.
- **Commercial Math**: Interest (Simple and Compound), Profit and Loss, Discount concepts.
- **Mensuration**: Perimeter and area of circles, rectangles, triangles; volumes of standard 3D solids.
- **Time, Work & Distance**: Ratio of work efficiency, time and distance, relative speed.

### 4. Part D: Hindi Syllabus (Alternative to English)
- **वर्तनी की सामान्य अशुद्धियाँ तथा शब्दों के शब्द रूप** (Spelling corrections and word forms)
- **पर्यायवाची तथा विलोम शब्द** (Synonyms and Antonyms)
- **मुहावरे और लोकोक्तियाँ** (Idioms and Proverbs with contextual meanings)
- **अनेक शब्दों के लिए एक शब्द** (One-word substitutions)
- **वाक्य शुद्धि** (Error spotting and sentence correction)
- **रिक्त स्थानों की पूर्ति** (Fill in the blanks with appropriate prepositions and nouns)
- **अपठित गद्यांश** (Reading comprehension passage with 5 direct questions)

## CAPF Force Preference Recommendation (Best to Safest)

1. **SSF (Secretariat Security Force)**: Stationed in New Delhi at Central Secretariat ministries. Regular office hours, weekends off, zero field hardship.
2. **CISF (Central Industrial Security Force)**: Stationed at airports, metro networks, space stations (ISRO), and major industrial plants. Urban posting with family accommodation.
3. **SSB (Sashastra Seema Bal)**: Deployed on peaceful international borders (Nepal and Bhutan). Friendly terrain with lower conflict levels.
4. **ITBP (Indo-Tibetan Border Police)**: High-altitude deployment along the Tibetan border (Ladakh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal). High risk-hardship allowance.
5. **BSF (Border Security Force)**: Deployed along Pakistan and Bangladesh international borders. High pride, defensive border guarding.
6. **CRPF (Central Reserve Police Force)**: Internal security, counter-insurgency, election duties across India. Highly active operational life.
7. **Assam Rifles (AR)**: Deployed in North-Eastern states; operates directly under Army operational control.

## 60-Day High-Output Study Schedule

- **Days 1 to 20 (Foundation & Daily 5km Jogging)**: Master arithmetic formulas (Percentage, Ratio, Profit & Loss) and Hindi grammar rules. Start 3 km morning jogs to build stamina.
- **Days 21 to 40 (Sectional Tests & Speed Drills)**: Solve 40 questions of reasoning and math daily. Increase running to 5 km continuous jogging at easy pace.
- **Days 41 to 50 (Full-Length Mocks)**: Take one full mock test daily at the exact time slot of your CBE. Target solving 65+ questions accurately in 50 minutes.
- **Days 51 to 60 (Revision & Peak Physical Fitness)**: Review all mistake formulas in your error notebook, memorize current affairs, and run 5 km under 23 minutes on alternate days.
